metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bar Nunn, WY | Natrona County
metaDescription: Bar Nunn, WY sits just north of Casper near the historic Salt Creek trend. Get a courthouse-checked read on your mineral interest before you consider an offer.
heroLead: Bar Nunn grew up as a bedroom community for Casper, but it sits close enough to the Salt Creek trend that I check every tract here individually before saying whether it's inside active production.
intro: Salt Creek anchors this part of Natrona County, and its reach has shifted over a hundred-plus years of development, some sections in continuous production, others leased and released without ever seeing a rig. Bar Nunn's proximity to Casper means a lot of what I run into is fractional interest inherited through several generations of the same family, sometimes without the current owner even knowing it exists.
If you got a letter from a landman, or found an old lease in a filing cabinet, send it my way and I'll tell you plainly what it means for your specific quarter section.

sections.heading: Where Bar Nunn sits relative to Salt Creek
paragraphs: Depending on the exact section, Bar Nunn-area minerals can sit inside an active Salt Creek unit or well outside it. That single fact changes everything about how I'd price your interest, since a producing tract with royalty history is a fundamentally different asset than undeveloped acreage nearby.
I run this check against Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission unit records before I ever quote a number, so you're not guessing based on your neighbor's situation.

sections.heading: Family fractional interests
paragraphs: It's common around here for a mineral interest to have split among three or four heirs, each holding a small fraction of a quarter section. I can work from a partial deed or an old probate order to reconstruct exactly what share you hold before we discuss any number.

Bar Nunn's growth as a residential area over the past couple of decades means a lot of these old mineral fractions have simply been forgotten by younger family members who never lived on the original ranch. If that's your situation, I'm used to starting from very little and building the ownership picture from scratch.

faqs.question: Is my Bar Nunn property inside the Salt Creek unit?
faqs.answer: It depends on your exact legal description. I'll check it against current unit boundaries before answering.

faqs.question: I got an unsolicited offer letter. Should I trust the number?
faqs.answer: Not without checking it independently. I'll give you a comparison based on actual county records and recent trades.

faqs.question: What if my interest is a small fraction shared with siblings?
faqs.answer: That's common. I can quote your specific fractional share, and coordinate with co-owners if everyone wants to sell together.

faqs.question: How do I start if I only have a family name and no paperwork?
faqs.answer: That's often enough. I can search the Natrona County recorder's grantor-grantee index using a name alone.
